title: Rare-event prefetch signal fusion handbook
author: Priya Nair
body:
Summary:
This handbook captures the operational design, telemetry contracts, decision matrices, and operator runbook for fusing sparse/rare-event signals used by the platform prefetch layer. It focuses on signal hygiene, fusion algorithms, alert thresholds, simulation/validation steps, and safe rollback patterns. The audience is platform operators, runtime engineers, and SREs responsible for LLM prefetch, KV prefix caches, and warmset orchestration.

Why this exists:
- Prefetch effectiveness is critical for tail-latency and token-cost economics but depends on low-volume signals (user cohorts, bursty tenants, cold prefixes) that are noisy and easy to misinterpret.
- Incorrect fusion or aggressive prefetches cause capacity blowouts, billing surprises, or cache thrash. This handbook defines how we collect, fuse, test, and act on rare signals safely.

Scope and definitions:
- Rare-event signal: any telemetry event that occurs at <1% of typical request rate for a model/tenant combination in a 1-hour window (examples: new prompt templates, one-off tenants, spike in long-context requests).
- Prefetch cohort: a set of prefixes/keys grouped by similarity heuristics and TTL for prefetching/warming.
- Fusion layer: the orchestration service that combines many low-volume signals into a prefetch decision (service name: prefetch-fusion-service).

Owner and duties:
- Service owner: eng-platform/prefetch team (primary: Priya Nair)
- On-call: Platform runtime on-call rotation (pager duty: pref-fusion-prod)
- Primary responders: prefetch-service-owners, runtime-ops
- Escalation: if service SLOs breached for >15m escalate to eng-plat leads and runtime reliability.

Telemetry contract (required metrics and labels):
- metric: prefetch.decisions.total (counter) -- tags: model, region, tenant_id, cohort_id, origin_signal
- metric: prefetch.decisions.approved (counter) -- tags same as above
- metric: prefetch.requests.success (counter)
- metric: prefetch.requests.fail (counter)
- metric: prefetch.token-cost.estimate (gauge) -- per-cohort estimated tokens consumed for prefetches in last 1m
- metric: prefetch.hit-rate.by-prefix (ratio) -- numerator: hits served from KV; denominator: prefetches attempted
- log: prefetch.decision_trace (structured JSON lines) -- fields: trace_id, cohort_id, signals[], fused_score, action (prefetch|skip|defer), operator_override
- sample span name: prefetch-fusion.evaluate (latency ms)

Signal categories and quality checks (fusion inputs):
1) Direct signals (high confidence): tenant-commit, canary flag, admin-trigger. These should be fused with strong positive weight.
2) Behavioral signals (medium confidence): repeated exact-prefix requests by same tenant, warmup requests sourced from integration test runners.
3) Heuristic signals (low confidence): similarity to hot prefixes, lexical clustering of prompts.
4) External indicators (contextual): product-release windows, scheduled demos, marketing events.

Each incoming signal must pass a minimal quality gate before being considered:
- timestamp freshness <= 10m
- schema validation (required fields present)
- minimum supporting count: direct signals pass with 1, behavioral and heuristic require >=3 events in rolling 10m window, or a model-backed similarity score >=0.85.

Fusion algorithm (high level):
- Normalized scoring: map each signal type to a calibrated score in [0,1]. Maintain running Bayesian prior per-cohort to avoid early overconfidence.
- Decay window: apply exponential decay to older signals (half-life configurable per cohort, default 30m).
- Cross-tenant dampening: if prefetch CPU target in region >70% reduce fusion acceptance threshold by +0.2.
- Cost cap: do not schedule prefetches that would increase estimated token-cost for a tenant by >5% of their last 24h spend without explicit approval.

Decision matrix (operator-friendly):
- fused_score >= 0.9 -> auto-prefetch (safe-path: spare burst capacity must be available)
- 0.6 <= fused_score < 0.9 -> staged-prefetch (deferred, sample 2% of replicas, soft-evict after 10m)
- 0.3 <= fused_score < 0.6 -> observe-only (create synthetic metric, do not prefetch)
- fused_score < 0.3 -> ignore

Safe-guards and SLOs:
- SLO: prefetch-fusion-service availability >= 99.95% monthly
- SLO: no more than 3 unexpected prefetch-related region degradations / quarter
- Safety budget (operator-managed): daily prefetch token budget per-region (default 5% of total runtime token consumption). Hitting 80% triggers an alert and automatically raises fusion thresholds.

Alerting and dashboards (what to monitor):
- Alert: PREFETCH_BUDGET_HIGH -> when prefetch.token-cost.estimate (region) > 80% of budget (severity: P2)
- Alert: PREFETCH_FAILURE_SPIKE -> prefetch.requests.fail rate >5% of attempts for 5m and absolute fails >50 (severity: P1)
- Alert: PREFETCH_HIT_RATE_DROP -> prefetch.hit-rate.by-prefix drops below 20% for a cohort for 10m (severity: P2)
- Dashboard widgets to create:
  - Prefetch budget burn-rate (by region, 1h/6h/24h)
  - Fusion score distribution (histogram)
  - Sampled decision_trace table (last 500 traces, searchable)
  - Correlation matrix: cohort prefetch vs tail-latency improvement vs token-cost delta

Operator runbook (step-by-step):
1) Receive alert (type) and check SLO impact on the platform incident board.
2) Query decision traces for the cohort: 
   - CLI: curl -s "https://prefetch.fusion.internal/api/v1/decisions?cohort_id=<COHORT>&limit=200" | jq '.results[] | {trace_id, fused_score, action, signals}'
3) Inspect metrics: prefetch.token-cost.estimate, prefetch.hit-rate.by-prefix, downstream tail latency for impacted model route (metric: llm.route.tail_latency_ms.99).
4) If PREFETCH_BUDGET_HIGH and fused_score_mean < 0.7: scale fusion threshold up by 0.15 (config path: /ops/prefetch/config -> key: fusion.threshold.override.region.<region>) and issue an operator annotation in the decision trace (see CLI below).
   - CLI snippet to apply override (kube exec to config service): kubectl -n ops exec svc/prefetch-config -- /bin/prefctl set region <region> fusion.threshold.override 0.85 --reason "operator budget intervention"
5) If PREFETCH_FAILURE_SPIKE: rollback latest prefetch rollout (if a rollout is in progress) or disable auto-prefetch for the affected cohort: curl -X POST -d '{"cohort_id":"<COHORT>","action":"disable_autoprefetch"}' https://prefetch.fusion.internal/api/v1/admin
6) If PREFETCH_HIT_RATE_DROP: mark cohort for observation and create a synthetic experiment (sampled staged-prefetch disabled) and open an investigation ticket with owner: prefetch-team. Include recent decision_traces.
7) Post-incident: run the regression check (see validation section) and either clear operator overrides or schedule a change request if the change is permanent.

Operator CLI utilities and snippets:
- decision trace fetcher: prefetchctl traces --cohort <id> --last 1h --format json
- apply operator annotation: prefetchctl annotate --trace <trace_id> --note "operator: budget bump" --severity low
- simulate fusion locally: docker run --rm prefetch-sim:latest --signals-file sample_signals.json --params fusion_config.yaml

Validation and canary tests (pre-deploy checklist for changes to fusion):
1) Unit tests for scoring maps and decay math.
2) Integration test: simulate 10k synthetic rare-events and assert false-positive prefetch rate <1%.
3) Canary model test: enable new fusion config on 1% of replicas for 24h and capture the following regression metrics: downstream tail_latency_99, prefetch.token-cost delta, prefetch.hit-rate.
4) Chaos test: run a simulated region capacity stress while canary is active to validate cross-tenant dampening reacts and auto-scales thresholds.

Configuration examples (YAML):
---
cohort_defaults:
  decay_half_life_minutes: 30
  min_support_count: 3
  max_daily_token_budget_fraction: 0.05
  staged_prefetch_sample_rate: 0.02
fusion_weights:
  direct: 1.0
  behavioral: 0.6
  heuristic: 0.3
  external: 0.2
fusion.thresholds:
  auto_prefetch: 0.9
  staged_prefetch: 0.6
  observe_only: 0.3
---

Simulation validation checklist (operator playbook):
- Run the sim for 48h with a 10x spike in rare-events and examine budget burn and false positives.
- Confirm that cross-tenant dampening reduces staged_prefetch and that region budget alerting triggers at 80% consumption.
- Verify decision_trace sampling rate (default 0.1%) is sufficient; increase to 1% for deeper debugging if needed.

Retrospective template (for post-incident reviews):
- Incident name and timeline
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence (decision_traces, metric deltas)
- What went well: operator interventions that limited blast radius
- What went wrong: gaps in telemetry, unexpected correlated signals
- Action items (owner, due date)

Appendix: known pitfalls and mitigations
- Pitfall: Similarity heuristics drift after tokenizer changes -> Mitigation: require a retrain of lexical clusters when tokenization library changes and run a drift detection daily.
- Pitfall: Marketing events flood heuristic signals -> Mitigation: ingestion of external calendar signals with high-priority tag that forces staged-prefetch only.
- Pitfall: Decision_trace storage growth -> Mitigation: cap trace retention to 90 days and sample aggressively for low-score traces.

Key contacts:

End.
